title: Tariffs on Imported Beverages in 2026: What the Midterms Change
summary: Aluminum tariffs are raising can costs for small drinks brands. What the 2026 midterms change, and what to check before signing 2027 contracts.
body_markdown:
Democrats take Congress in January. Existing aluminum tariffs remain in place, and small drinks brands are planning their 2027 can deals now.


On Tuesday, Democrats[won both the House and the Senate](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/live-blog/midterm-election-results-2026-news-trump-live-updates-rcna605763) . In Canada, the head of the aluminum industry said he is[more optimistic than ever](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/canadian-aluminum-industry-sees-hope-185504446.html) . For a small drinks brand signing next year's can contract this month, the question is simpler: will any of this lower the price of a can?


## The Cost Moved to the Can


American buyers pay the global aluminum price plus the Midwest Premium, a benchmark reflecting delivery costs, tariffs, and US supply and demand. It[passed $1 a pound in January](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/012626-us-aluminum-trade-uncertainty-supply-tightness-push-midwest-premium-above-1lb) . The Brewers Association estimated in August that tariffs accounted for[roughly 30% of the delivered primary aluminum price](https://www.brewersassociation.org/government-affairs-updates/from-tariff-to-tap-how-aluminum-costs-reach-brewers/) . That is the metal price, not the price of a finished can.


Buying American does not automatically avoid the pressure. US-made cans, including those made with recycled metal, are exposed to connected aluminum markets. Cans carried[nearly 80% of craft beer volume sold in stores in 2025](https://www.brewersassociation.org/government-affairs-updates/from-tariff-to-tap-how-aluminum-costs-reach-brewers/) .


## Same Can, Different Price


Big brands can negotiate large orders. Small brands have less purchasing power and less room to pass higher packaging costs to customers.


The number of breweries[fell 1.8% in the year to June 2026](https://www.brewersassociation.org/association-news/2026-midyear-report-pressure-persists-as-signs-of-stability-emerge/) , and craft distilleries saw[closures outpace openings](https://www.brewbound.com/news/craft-distillery-closures-outpace-openings-as-volume-falls-8) . Weaker demand is already a problem. More expensive packaging adds another pressure.


## Where the Cash Goes


Some small brands[buy in bulk to manage costs](https://www.waff.com/2026/10/27/tariffs-cold-one-huntsville-brewers-face-rising-can-costs/) . Their next contracts could lock in today’s prices.


Take an illustrative brand buying 2 million empty cans a year at 12 cents each: $240,000. A 25% price rise makes that $300,000. Buy six months upfront and $150,000 goes out at once instead of $25,000 a month. Compared with buying monthly, an extra $125,000 initially sits in cans for the next five months. This example excludes storage and financing costs.


Illustrative example. Same six-month can cost; different timing of cash payments.


## What the Vote Changes, and When


The new Congress starts in January. But the election itself does not remove the president’s aluminum tariffs. A repeal bill can be vetoed, and[overriding a veto takes two-thirds of members voting in each chamber](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/RS/PDF/RS22654/RS22654.9.pdf) , with a quorum present. Neither party’s projected seats give it that margin on its own.


A deal with Canada is another possible path. Canada accounted for[70% of US primary aluminum imports in 2024](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/121525-aluminum-us-midwest-premium-reaches-90-centslb-for-the-first-time) . Prices already react to that possibility. In August, the premium[fell sharply on reports of possible tariff reductions](https://www.brewersassociation.org/government-affairs-updates/from-tariff-to-tap-how-aluminum-costs-reach-brewers/) for certain Canadian aluminum.


Relief may come. Whether it arrives before your 2027 can contract is signed remains uncertain.


## Before The Next Order


**Your 2027 contract.** A fixed price protects you if costs rise but can shut you out of a fall. A shorter term or a price tied to a benchmark can leave room for relief, while also exposing you to increases. Check which costs the formula actually covers.


**Your cash.** How much does a bulk order tie up, and for how long?
